newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong councillors lash leader Tung's changes.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong councillors lash leader Tung's changes.

text.p: Elected local government councillors in Hong Kong vented outrage on Thursday that future leader Tung Chee-hwa had appointed defeated election candidates to serve on enlarged councils after China takes over on Tuesday.
Eight councillors from Hong Kong's Central and Western districts sent a protest note to Tung saying the public opposed the move and demanding he explain how he decided on the change.
There was no immediate reaction from Tung's office.
Members argued that elections would become a farce if both winners and losers get seats on the councils. People would not bother to vote again if this happened, they said.
One of the protesting councillors, Kam Nai-wai, said Tung's move was a step backwards for Hong Kong democracy.
Another, Yuen Bun-keung, said if there must be a system of appointing councillors, those selected should be people who have contributed to the districts, not an arbitrary choice.

Tung last week added 96 appointed seats to Hong Kong's 18 district boards which advise the government on local government issues, an expansion of 25 percent. The beneficiaries are pro-Beijing personalities defeated in the last local elections.
A further nine were appointed to the Urban Council and 11 to the Regional Council which perform municipal government roles in Hong Kong and the rural New Territories area.
